gen-gf-snowburst-one-gf-sintony: Stencil cuts and tall lowercase give Snowburst One a loud, expressive face, with wide bridges breaking up every letter. Sintony follows in a plain sans, chunky through the middle and smooth on every curve.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-stack-sans-notch: Tektur draws its curves with generous openings and a pipe-cleaner look, and its lowercase runs oversized and distinctive. Stack Sans Notch is the one to read, its sans-serif curves letting you see right inside.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-sulphur-point: Commanding tube-like strokes define Tilt Neon, with a large x-height and short ascenders giving it weight. And Sulphur Point brings a steady, marker-like line in sans-serif form, its gaps in c, e, s and a distinct.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-stack-sans-headline: Unica One has a very large lowercase eye and daylight inside every curve. It earns its keep big and short, while Stack Sans Headline carries the rest with a deep middle band and a monoline skeleton, a plain sans with approachable manners.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-stack-sans-text: Warnes lets its ink strokes taper out before they touch, with no contrast at all. Stack Sans Text meets that stretched, spacious tracking with a marker-like constant line, big-bodied lowercase and sans-serif curve endings kept well apart.
gen-irish-grover-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans reads like it was drawn with a ruler, constant in width. Irish Grover above it is the opposite, fun and organic, its tall lowercase making words look sturdy while its strokes swell very slightly, so paragraphs of the sans feel steady and filled out.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-yaldevi: Loud, cheerful and poured at one width, Luckiest Guy sets its mean line high. Yaldevi, a sans with outsized lowercase and an e that opens clearly to the right, is the one that holds up when text gets long.
gen-megrim-gf-ubuntu-sans: Ubuntu Sans reads modern, with washer-big lowercase eyes and tubular strokes like bent copper pipe. Megrim, meanwhile, goes angular and futuristic above it, every stroke ending at the same measured thickness and its skyward x-height line pulling the eye up.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-sofia-sans: Bookish and a little nostalgic, Mystery Quest opens its jaws on every curve and tucks compact ascenders over tall lowercase. And Sofia Sans, a sans-serif with no thick-and-thin modulation at all, is the pair's strongest card, standing tall like cut stencil pieces.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-sulphur-point: Press Start 2P is fun and retro, with big open-looking bowls and letters pinned far apart like cut-outs. Sulphur Point, a sans with distinct gaps and curves that never thin at the turns, is the better reader.
